bach_wtc1_prelude_01_c_major_piano.theorySummary: 35-bar masterclass in harmonic voice leading over unbroken arpeggios: opens with a textbook C bass pedal (I–ii7–V7–I), modulates clockwise to G Major (V), descends chromatically through diminished & borrowed minor color, and rests over an 8-bar G dominant pedal before a plagal coda.

studyGuide.vibeAndSound: Shimmering, harp-like broken chords across 35 steady bars—every measure changes harmonic pressure by shifting just one or two notes smoothly by step.
studyGuide.harmonyHook: A living textbook of Circle of Fifths gravity, 3rd-inversion 7th chords (7th in the bass forcing a half-step drop), chromatic inner voices, and pedal-point suspense.
practiceTips: Play just the two-note left-hand shapes in Bars 1–4 first to hear how C stays anchored in the bass while Dm7/C steps down to G7/B and back to C.
Trace the chromatic descent in Bars 12–15 (G → Gm → Dm/F → Fm → C/E): one inner voice falls half-step by half-step (B → B♭ → A → A♭ → G).
Notice Bars 24–31 all sit on a G bass pedal—tension builds right over the dominant bass before resolving in Bar 32.

sections.title: 1. Opening C Pedal
sections.progressionTag: C – Dm7/C – G7/B – C
sections.insight: Anchors C Major with a textbook I–ii7–V7–I turnaround over a stationary C pedal in Bars 1–2 before leading-tone B steps back home.

sections.title: 2. Modulation to G (V)
sections.progressionTag: Am – D7/C – G/B – Cmaj7/B – Am7 – D7 – G
sections.insight: Pivots through vi (Am) and introduces borrowed F♯ in D7/C (V7/V) to tonicize G Major cleanly via a descending C → B → A bass walk.

sections.title: 3. Chromatic Descent Home
sections.progressionTag: Gm – Dm/F – Fm – C/E – Fmaj7/E – Dm – G – C
sections.insight: Melts G Major back to C Major by flattening B to B♭ (Gm) and A to A♭ (Fm), letting the bass walk smoothly down F → E → D → G → C.

sections.title: 4. V7/IV & Diminished Tension
sections.progressionTag: C7 – F – F♯dim – Fm/A♭ – G7
sections.insight: Adds B♭ to turn C into V7/IV (pushing to F), then squeezes F → F♯ → A♭ toward the G7 dominant cadence.

sections.title: 5. Dominant G Pedal & Coda
sections.progressionTag: C/G – G7 – Cm/G – C/G – G7 – C – F – Cmaj7 – C
sections.insight: Suspends C/G, G7, and even minor Cm/G over an unbroken G bass pedal before resolving to C and adding a gentle IV → I plagal sigh.

1.cardSummary: Sets C Major home; launches C bass pedal
1.whatItDoes: Grounds the C Major tonic (I) in root position—bright, settled, and open—while setting up the 2-bar C bass drone.
1.biggerPicture: Opens Section 1 ('Opening C Pedal', Bars 1–4) as the stable baseline for a classic I → ii7 → V7 → I turnaround.
1.whyItWorks: Locks in scale degrees 1–3–5 (C · E · G) and keeps C in the bass into Bar 2 so the harmonic shift feels effortless.

2.cardSummary: 7th (C) in bass leans down toward G7/B
2.whatItDoes: Pre-dominant ii7 (Dm7/C) puts its dissonant 7th (C) directly in the bass (3rd inversion), creating forward lean rather than rest.
2.biggerPicture: Bridges home C (Bar 1) to dominant G7/B (Bar 3) as step 2 of the opening ii–V–I progression.
2.whyItWorks: Holds C from Bar 1 as a pedal bass; because C is Dm7's 7th, gravity pulls it down a half-step to B while D and F carry smoothly into G7/B.

3.cardSummary: Leading-tone bass B pulls a half-step to C
3.whatItDoes: Dominant V7 (G7/B) places C Major's leading tone (B) right in the bass (1st inversion) alongside the urgent B–F tritone.
3.biggerPicture: Climaxes the opening I → ii7 → V7 → I phrase right before resolving home in Bar 4.
3.whyItWorks: G7's tritone pulls symmetrically inward (B rises a half-step to C while F drops a half-step to E), completing a smooth C → B → C bass neighbor line.

6.whatItDoes: Secondary dominant V7/V (D7/C) introduces F♯ outside C Major, with the 7th (C) in the bass demanding downward resolution.
6.biggerPicture: Pivots Section 2 away from Am (Bar 5) toward a temporary key center on G Major (V) across Bars 7–11.
6.whyItWorks: D7's tritone (F♯ and C) pulls straight into G/B (F♯ rises a half-step to G while C steps down to B) on a falling C → B bass line.

20.cardSummary: Adds B♭ to aim straight at F (IV)
20.whatItDoes: Turns stable tonic C into secondary dominant C7 (V7/IV) by introducing borrowed B♭, destabilizing home base.
20.biggerPicture: Launches Section 4's dramatic climb: V7/IV (C7) → IV (F) → ♯iv° (F♯dim) → iv (Fm/A♭) → V7 (G7).
20.whyItWorks: C7's E–B♭ tritone pulls straight into F Major (E steps up to F while B♭ drops a half-step to A), resolving counter-clockwise by 5th.

28.cardSummary: Darkens C/G with E♭ over the G pedal
28.whatItDoes: Temporarily swaps major E for parallel-minor E♭ (Cm/G) while keeping the insistent G dominant bass ringing below.
28.biggerPicture: Adds a poignant shadow right in the middle of the 8-bar G dominant pedal (Bars 24–31) before brightening back to C/G.
28.whyItWorks: Chromatic voice leading (E → E♭ → E) creates intense longing over the stationary G bass without changing the chord's dominant-pedal anchor.

chopin_prelude_op28_no20_c_minor_piano.theorySummary: 13-bar Romantic harmony jewel in C Minor: opens with a solemn funeral-march cadence (i–iv7–V–i), sequences it down a major 3rd to A♭ (VI), descends down a 6-note chromatic bass line (C–B–B♭–A–A♭–G) under diminished & tritone-sub tension, and whispers an unforgettable pp echo.

studyGuide.vibeAndSound: Heavy, orchestral piano block chords marching in dotted rhythms—opening ff like a funeral procession before dropping to p and a ghostly pp echo.
studyGuide.harmonyHook: Packs four chords per bar so every beat shifts voice leading: sequential transposition (Cm → A♭), a 6-step chromatic bass walk, and tritone-like A♭7 → G7 tension.
practiceTips: Notice how Bar 2 copies Bar 1's exact chord shape (i → iv7 → V → i) starting on A♭ (VI) instead of Cm (i).
Trace the slow chromatic bass descent across Bars 5–6: C → B → B♭ → A → A♭ → G.
Compare Bars 9–12 (pp) against Bars 5–8 (p)—same aching descent, transformed purely by soft dynamics and register.

sections.title: 1. Funeral March & A♭ Sequence
sections.progressionTag: Cm – A♭ – G7 – D7/G
sections.insight: States a full minor cadence inside Bar 1, sequences it down to A♭ (VI) in Bar 2, drives through V7/iv (C7 → Fm) in Bar 3, and pauses on a dramatic half cadence in Bar 4.

sections.title: 2. Chromatic Bass Descent (p)
sections.progressionTag: Cm – Bm – Gm/B♭ – Am7 – A♭7 – G7 – Cm
sections.insight: Glides down a chromatic bass staircase (C → B → B♭ → A → A♭ → G) in Bars 5–6, resolving via a tight Bar 7 cadence and Bar 8 Neapolitan D♭ → G7 → Cm turn.

sections.title: 3. Whispered Echo (pp) & Finale
sections.progressionTag: Bm – Gm/B♭ – Am7 – A♭7 – G7 – Cm
sections.insight: Replays the chromatic descent at a hushed pp before settling onto one bare, solemn C Minor final chord in Bar 13.

1.cardSummary: Full i–iv7–V–i funeral cadence in 1 bar
1.whatItDoes: Grounds C Minor (i) while packing four distinct block chords (Cm → Fm7 → G → Cm) into four march beats.
1.biggerPicture: Establishes the dark tonic cadence motif in Section 1 that Bar 2 immediately transposes into A♭ Major.
1.whyItWorks: Keeping C on top and in the outer voice frame lets the inner chord tones cycle smoothly from subdominant warmth (Fm7) through harmonic-minor leading tone B (G) back to Cm.

2.cardSummary: Transposes Bar 1's cadence down into A♭
2.whatItDoes: Opens on warm submediant A♭ (VI) and cycles A♭ → D♭ → E♭7 → A♭, momentarily visiting A♭ Major as a mini key.
2.biggerPicture: Answers Bar 1's C Minor phrase with a major-key sequential echo a major 3rd lower.
2.whyItWorks: Shares C and E♭ with Cm so the sudden leap to A♭ feels cohesive, while E♭7's G–D♭ tritone cleanly cadences onto A♭.

5.cardSummary: Starts chromatic bass walk C → B → B♭
5.whatItDoes: Lands on C Minor (i) from Bar 4's dominant, then immediately slips down via Bm and Gm/B♭ to start a long lament bass.
5.biggerPicture: Opens Section 2's tender piano (p) chromatic descent spanning Bars 5–6 before Bar 7's cadence.
5.whyItWorks: Each beat drops the bass exactly one half-step (C → B → B♭) while holding G on top as a common melodic anchor.

6.cardSummary: Chromatic A → A♭ → G bass lands on G7
6.whatItDoes: Continues the falling bass from Bar 5 (Am7 → A♭7 → G7 → G7/F), adding raised 6th A and borrowed A♭7 color before V7.
6.biggerPicture: Climaxes the 2-bar chromatic bass lament (C–B–B♭–A–A♭–G) and sets up Bar 7's resolution onto Cm/E♭.
6.whyItWorks: A♭7 sits one half-step above G7 (a tritone-sub style push) before stepping down onto G7/F, whose 7th (F) pulls downward to E♭ in Bar 7.

schubert_moments_musicaux_op94_no3_d780_.theorySummary: 78-bar Viennese miniature in F Minor: alternates plaintive minor dance themes with Dorian IV7 (B♭7) lifts, sunlit A♭ / D♭ major episodes, and a magical Bar 68 Picardy third modulation to F Major that glows peacefully to the end.

studyGuide.vibeAndSound: Light, folk-like 2/4 staccato accompaniment under a wistful, singing melody—playful yet bittersweet, ending with an unexpected ray of F Major sunshine.
studyGuide.harmonyHook: Showcases modal color in F Minor: raised Dorian 6th (B♭7 = IV7), smooth relative-major detours to A♭ (III) and D♭ (VI), and a Picardy-third ending in F Major.
practiceTips: Notice how Bar 3 uses B♭7 (major IV7 with D♮) instead of B♭m (iv)—that single raised note gives Schubert's melody its signature sweet-sour ache.
Hear how Bars 19–34 step sideways into bright A♭ Major (III) and D♭ Major (VI) before C7 pulls everything back to F Minor.
Listen closely at Bars 65–68: Am (♯iii) nudges the ear up toward F Major so the final 11 bars bloom in pure major.

sections.title: 1. F Minor Dance & Dorian B♭7
sections.progressionTag: Fm – B♭7 – A♭ – A♭maj7 – Fm
sections.insight: Establishes the bouncing F Minor accompaniment and spotlights raised-6th Dorian color (B♭7) sliding through relative major A♭ back to Fm.

sections.title: 2. Relative A♭ & D♭ Major Lift
sections.progressionTag: A♭ – D♭maj7 – A♭add9 – B♭add9 – E♭7 – C7
sections.insight: Moves cleanly into bright A♭ Major (III) and D♭maj7 (VImaj7) before C7 (V7) reasserts F Minor's dominant pull.

sections.title: 3. Minor Reprise & G7/B Pivot
sections.progressionTag: Fm/C – C7 – A♭7 – B♭m/D♭ – Fm – Edim/B♭ – G7/B
sections.insight: Alternates dark Fm/C–C7 tension with warm A♭–Fm reprises before Edim/B♭ and G7/B (V7/V) build dramatic harmonic suspense.

sections.title: 4. Picardy F Major Finale
sections.progressionTag: Am/C – F – C7/F – E♭dim7 – F
sections.insight: Flips from F Minor into radiant F Major (Picardy turn) at Bar 68, lingering gently over C7/F pedal tensions until the final major triad.

3.cardSummary: Raised D♮ turns iv into sweet-sour B♭7
3.whatItDoes: Substitutes bright major-quality Dorian IV7 (B♭7) for natural minor iv (B♭m), introducing D♮ outside F Minor.
3.biggerPicture: Gives Section 1's opening dance theme its signature Schubertian lift before stepping smoothly into A♭ (III) in Bar 4.
3.whyItWorks: D♮ creates a buoyant half-step neighbor motion back toward D♭/C while sharing F and A♭ with the surrounding F Minor / A♭ chords.

68.cardSummary: Miraculous shift from F Minor to F Major
68.whatItDoes: Replaces dark A♭ with radiant A♮, turning the home key from F Minor into pure, sunlit F Major (I).
68.biggerPicture: Launches the final 11-bar F Major coda (Bars 68–78) where all earlier minor shadows dissolve.
68.whyItWorks: Bars 65–67 gently prepared A♮ inside Am (♯iii), so arriving on F Major feels both surprising and deeply earned.

tarrega_lagrima_guitar_both.theorySummary: 32-bar romantic guitar miniature in binary A–A–B–B form: contrasts singing E Major harmony (Eadd9, 3-bar B7 tension, deceptive vi7, V7/V) in the A section against a tender parallel E Minor flip in the B section.

studyGuide.vibeAndSound: Delicate, tear-drop fingerstyle waltz—crystal-clear upper melody singing on the high E string over soft thumb accompaniment.
studyGuide.harmonyHook: Teaches parallel-key contrast (E Major vs. E Minor) alongside a textbook deceptive cadence (B7 → C♯m7/B) and V7/V chromatic climb.
practiceTips: In Bars 2–4, notice how B7 holds for three bars while the bass quietly alternates F♯ and D♯/E♭ to keep momentum alive.
Listen at Bar 5: instead of resolving B7 home to E, Tárrega surprises you with C♯m7/B (vi7) and walks the 7th B down in the bass.
Compare Bar 1's bright Eadd9 (G♯) against Bar 17's Em (G♮)—dropping that single note one fret transforms the entire mood.

sections.title: 1. A Section — Singing E Major
sections.progressionTag: Eadd9 – B7 – C♯m7/B – F♯m – F♯7/B♭ – Em
sections.insight: Pairs shimmering Eadd9 and 3-bar B7 tension with a deceptive vi7 twist (Bar 5) and secondary dominant F♯7/B♭ (V7/V) before dipping onto Em.

sections.title: 2. A Repeat — Lyric Echo
sections.progressionTag: Eadd9 – B7 – C♯m7/B – F♯m – F♯7/B♭ – Em
sections.insight: Repeats the E Major theme cleanly, reinforcing the B7 → C♯m7 deceptive cadence and smooth bass voice leading.

sections.title: 3. B Section — Parallel E Minor
sections.progressionTag: Em – B – Em – Bm7/F♯ – Em
sections.insight: Flips straight into parallel E Minor (i), pairing dark Em against major V (B) and modal minor v7 (Bm7/F♯) for melancholic contrast.

sections.title: 4. B Repeat — Quiet Minor Close
sections.progressionTag: Em – B – Em – Bm7/F♯ – Em
sections.insight: Repeats the aching E Minor phrase, easing from Bm7/F♯ through Em/G–Em/B inversions onto a serene final E Minor chord.

1.cardSummary: Eadd9 chimes open E–F♯ shimmer; turns to B7/E♭
1.whatItDoes: Opens E Major (I) with a bell-like F♯ (9th) above the triad before stepping to 1st-inversion B7/E♭ on beat 3.
1.biggerPicture: Establishes the singing waltz texture and launches the A section's opening 4-bar dominant tension arc.
1.whyItWorks: F♯ sits right next to G♯ on the high E/B strings for guitar resonance, while the bass slips down a half-step (E → D♯/E♭).

5.cardSummary: Surprises B7 by landing on C♯m7/B instead of E
5.whatItDoes: Instead of resolving 3 bars of B7 back to E, lands on relative minor C♯m7 (vi7) with its 7th (B) held in the bass.
5.biggerPicture: Creates a deceptive cadence that extends the 8-bar A section through F♯m (ii) and F♯7 (V7/V) instead of ending early.
5.whyItWorks: Holding B from B7 as a smooth pedal bass lets upper voices shift subtly to C♯m7, then step the bass down B → A into F♯m.

17.cardSummary: Lowers G♯ to G♮, turning E Major into Em
17.whatItDoes: Opens the B section in parallel E Minor (i), replacing bright G♯ with reflective G♮.
17.biggerPicture: Creates the classic A (Major) vs. B (Minor) emotional contrast that defines Lágrima ('Teardrop').
17.whyItWorks: Shares root E and 5th B with E Major, so changing only the 3rd by one fret shifts the mood instantly without jarring the ear.

villa_lobos_etude_1_guitar_both.theorySummary: 61-bar fingerstyle arpeggio showcase in E Minor: keeps the guitar's open E and B strings ringing while movable chromatic shapes, secondary dominants (E7 = V7/iv, F♯7 = V7/V), and symmetric diminished chords glide seamlessly up and down the neck.

studyGuide.vibeAndSound: Hypnotic, perpetual-motion 16th-note right-hand arpeggio stream—dark, driving Brazilian classical guitar counterpoint.
studyGuide.harmonyHook: Exploits open guitar strings (E and B) as resonant pedals underneath shifting chromatic chords, applied dominants (E7 → Am, F♯7 → B7), and sliding diminished bridges.
practiceTips: Keep your right-hand arpeggio pattern relaxed and mechanical so you can listen purely to the left hand walking up and down the bass strings.
Notice Bars 11–12 (E/A♭ → E/B) and 23–24 (E7): Villa-Lobos turns the tonic E into major/dominant V/iv to pull into A Minor (iv).
Spot the sliding diminished chords (Edim in Bars 31–32 & 37–38) gliding effortlessly against open E and B strings.

sections.title: 1. Open-String Pedal & V/iv Pull
sections.progressionTag: Em – Am/E – B7/F♯ – E/A♭ – Am – Em7
sections.insight: Locks the right-hand arpeggio pattern over Em and Am/E pedals, passes through B7, and brightens E to major (V/iv) to pull warmly into Am.

sections.title: 2. Climbing E7 & Diminished Slides
sections.progressionTag: Em/B – Bsus4 – B7 – E7 – C♯m/E – Am/E – Edim
sections.insight: Moves up the fretboard through B7 and E7 (V7/iv), visiting Dorian C♯m (♯vi) before unleashing shimmering Edim diminished tension.

sections.title: 3. High-Fret Tension & Bmaj7 Shift
sections.progressionTag: Am/E – E7 – Edim – Am/E – Em – Bmaj7/B♭
sections.insight: Repeats the E7–Edim–Am cycle higher up, then drops onto tonic Em and surprises the ear with lush Bmaj7 in Bar 46.

sections.title: 4. Circle Chain & Arpeggio Coda
sections.progressionTag: F♯7 – C♯m7 – F♯m – B7 – Em – Am/C – C♯m7/E
sections.insight: Drives a Circle-of-Fifths chain (F♯7 → B7 → Em) via C♯m7 and F♯m before resting across E Minor pedals and an open high harmonic/chordal finish.

11.cardSummary: Brightens Em to E (V/iv) aiming at Am
11.whatItDoes: Turns dark Em into bright E Major (with 3rd G♯/A♭ in the bass), transforming tonic into an active secondary dominant V/iv.
11.biggerPicture: Pulls the opening E Minor phrase up toward A Minor (iv) in Bar 13, breaking out of the tonic pedal.
11.whyItWorks: Raising G to G♯ creates a half-step leading tone straight into A, while keeping open high strings ringing over the fretted bass.

31.cardSummary: Edim slides tension against open E/B strings
31.whatItDoes: Stacks diminished minor 3rds (E · G · B♭) over the ringing arpeggio pattern, injecting sharp, rootless instability.
31.biggerPicture: Creates high-neck climax tension between E7 (Bar 30) and the resolving Am/E arrival (Bar 33).
31.whyItWorks: Diminished symmetry lets the left hand shift cleanly up the fingerboard while open guitar strings tie the sonority together.

47.cardSummary: F♯7 launches final Circle chain home
47.whatItDoes: Fires dominant F♯7 (V7/V) with its tritone (A♯ and E), stepping one fifth clockwise past B7.
47.biggerPicture: Launches the closing Circle-of-Fifths journey (F♯7 → … → B7 → Em) that brings the étude home.
47.whyItWorks: F♯7 steps counter-clockwise by 5th into B7 (after C♯m7–F♯m), setting up the final V7 → i resolution.

bee_gees_how_deep_is_your_love_guitar_bo.theorySummary: 74-bar pop-soul harmonic masterclass in B Major (played with Capo 2): blends lush maj7 tonic pedals (B → Bmaj7 → Emaj7/B), signature pop IV/5 dominant suspensions (Eadd9/F♯), secondary dominants (V7/vi, V7/V, V7/ii), borrowed ♭VII (A), and an iconic minor plagal cadence (Em → B).

studyGuide.vibeAndSound: Warm, glowing fingerstyle pop ballad (Capo 2)—open-string shapes let 7ths and add9s ring effortlessly like an electric piano.
studyGuide.harmonyHook: Classic 70s songwriting alchemy: substitutes lush IV/5 (Eadd9/F♯) for plain V7, tonicizes vi and ii with applied dominants, and seals every chorus with minor iv → I (Em → B).
practiceTips: Play Bars 1–3 slowly: B stays in the bass across B → Bmaj7 → Emaj7/B while the upper melody steps gently B → A♯ → G♯.
Feel how Eadd9/F♯ (Bars 12, 16) acts as a gentle, suspended dominant (IV over the 5th degree F♯) rather than a harsh F♯7.
Listen for the emotional peak at Bars 25 & 32: borrowing minor Em (iv) with G♮ softens the return to B Major—the signature minor plagal hook.

sections.title: 1. Intro & Verse 1 — B Pedal
sections.progressionTag: B – Bmaj7 – Emaj7/B – A♭m7/F♯ – B – F♯5
sections.insight: Drifts gently over a B bass pedal (B → Bmaj7 → Emaj7/B) and steps down through vi7/7th-in-bass (G♯m7/F♯) before F♯5 opens the pre-chorus.

sections.title: 2. Pre-Chorus — V7/vi & IV/5 Lift
sections.progressionTag: B/F♯ – E♭7 – C♯m – Eadd9/F♯ – B – A♭m7 – C♯m7 – E – C♯7/B
sections.insight: Uses D♯7/E♭7 (V7/vi) to lean into ii (C♯m), suspends IV/5 (Eadd9/F♯), and sparks a bright C♯7 (V7/V) lift toward the chorus.

sections.title: 3. Chorus — ♭VII & Minor Plagal Em→B
sections.progressionTag: C♯m7 – A – E♭m7/F♯ – B – Em – A♭7 – Eadd9 – Em – B
sections.insight: Swells with borrowed ♭VII (A), secondary dominant G♯7/A♭7 (V7/ii), and the iconic bittersweet minor plagal cadence Em (iv) → B (I).

sections.title: 4. Verse 2 & Chorus Reprise
sections.progressionTag: C♯m – E♭7 – Eadd9/F♯ – B – A – Em – B – F♯sus4
sections.insight: Returns through the shimmering pre-chorus and chorus hooks before suspending cleanly on F♯sus4 → F♯sus2 for the outro build.

sections.title: 5. Outro Chorus & Fade Cadence
sections.progressionTag: B – A♭m7/F♯ – Em – C♯m – A♭7 – Eadd9 – Em – B
sections.insight: Revisits the emotional Em (iv) and A♭7 (V7/ii) chorus climb one last time, settling through F♯sus4 → B5 onto pure B Major.

2.cardSummary: A♯ adds dreamy maj7 warmth over B bass
2.whatItDoes: Expands the B triad with its major 7th (A♯), softening tonic rest into warm, floating longing while holding B in the bass.
2.biggerPicture: Step 2 of the iconic 3-bar B pedal (B → Bmaj7 → Emaj7/B) that opens the verse.
2.whyItWorks: The melody descends just one half-step (B → A♯) over unchanged B–D♯–F♯ harmony, creating effortless emotional warmth.

12.cardSummary: Lush Eadd9 over F♯ bass acts as suspended V
12.whatItDoes: Voices the IV chord (Eadd9) over the dominant 5th degree (F♯) in the bass—a classic pop/gospel 'slash-dominant' sound.
12.biggerPicture: Bridges C♯m/E♭7 smoothly back into B Major in Bar 13 without needing a harsh F♯7.
12.whyItWorks: E, G♯, and B over F♯ act like F♯11 (9th, 11th, 13th), giving the tension of a dominant bass with the warmth of a IV chord.

20.cardSummary: Modal A Major drops a whole step below B
20.whatItDoes: Borrows A Major (♭VII) from Mixolydian/parallel minor, introducing out-of-key A♮ and E–C♯ color.
20.biggerPicture: Gives the chorus hook ('And you come to me...') its unexpected open lift between C♯m7 and D♯m7/F♯.
20.whyItWorks: Moving a whole step below tonic (A → B via E♭m7/F♯) sounds wider and gentler than a leading-tone dominant pull.

29.cardSummary: A♭7 (V7/ii) adds C♮ pull toward C♯m
29.whatItDoes: Turns diatonic G♯m7 (vi7) into bright dominant A♭7/G♯7 (V7/ii), introducing chromatic C♮ (B♯) outside B Major.
29.biggerPicture: Pushes the second half of the chorus through Eadd9 into C♯m (ii), elevating the emotional intensity before Em → B.
29.whyItWorks: Raising B to C♮ creates a classic tritone (C♮ and G♭/F♯) longing to resolve counter-clockwise by 5th toward C♯m.

32.cardSummary: Borrowed Em sighs softly home into B
32.whatItDoes: Flips IV to borrowed minor iv (Em, bringing chromatic G♮) mid-bar before resolving directly onto tonic B Major.
32.biggerPicture: Delivers the chorus's signature bittersweet pop cadence (iv → I), softening the return home.
32.whyItWorks: G♮ drops just one half-step to F♯ while B stays anchored as a shared tone—one of tonal music's warmest voice-leading sighs.

tommy_emmanuel_amazing_grace_guitar_both.theorySummary: 77-bar Tommy Emmanuel fingerstyle arrangement of the classic hymn in E Major (9/8): weaves gospel passing diminished chords (A♯°7, G♯°, Gdim7), secondary dominants (V7/IV, V7/V), 9ths/13ths, and a lush Phrygian tag (G6 → Fmaj7 → Emaj9).

studyGuide.vibeAndSound: Lilting, orchestral 9/8 fingerstyle hymn—builds from simple, vocal open chords in Verse 1 to sparkling gospel jazz voicings and harp harmonics.
studyGuide.harmonyHook: Shows how a 3-chord hymn (I–IV–V) transforms through jazz/gospel reharmonization: IV → ♯iv°7 → I/5 bass walks, iii° → IV7 approaches, and chromatic ♭III–♭II endings.
practiceTips: Count the gentle 9/8 sway (1-2-3, 4-5-6, 7-8-9) so the grace notes and inner bass walks breathe naturally.
Spot the gospel walk at Bars 4, 12, 20, and 60: Aadd9 → A♯dim7 → E/B steps the bass chromatically A → A♯ → B.
Explore Bars 73–77 at the very end: Tommy slides chromatically down G6 → Fmaj7 (♭III → ♭II) before landing on a glassy Emaj9.

sections.title: 1. Verse 1 — Gentle Hymn & A♯°7
sections.progressionTag: C♯m7 – E – Aadd9 – A♯dim7 – E7 – A – F♯9 – B7
sections.insight: Opens softly on vi7 (C♯m7) and bright E Major, introducing the gospel A → A♯°7 → E/B bass walk and V7/V (F♯9) → B7 turnaround.

sections.title: 2. Verse 2 — Gospel E7 → G♯° → A7
sections.progressionTag: E – C♯m7 – F♯m7 – B7 – E7 – G♯° – A7 – A♯dim7 – B7
sections.insight: Enriches the middle stanza with a rising chromatic dominant climb (E7 → G♯° → A7 → A♯dim7 → B6) that drives forward into Bar 33.

sections.title: 3. Verse 3 — Singing High Melody
sections.insight: Lifts the melody higher with airy E6, E9 (V7/IV), A6, and G♯7 → C♯m7 → G13 color substitutions.

sections.title: 4. Verse 4 — Jazz Extensions & Turnarounds
sections.progressionTag: E6 – E7/G♯ – A – E7/B – Gdim7 – B9/F♯ – G♯° – A7
sections.insight: Deepens the hymn with E7/G♯, chromatic passing Gdim7 and Cdim7 chords, and rich F♯9 → C9 tritone color.

sections.title: 5. Ending — ♭III–♭II Phrygian Tag
sections.progressionTag: C♯m7 – F♯9 – B7 – Asus2 – G6 – Fmaj7 – Emaj9 – Emaj7
sections.insight: Winds down softly, then slips through borrowed G6 (♭III) and Fmaj7 (♭II) before blooming onto a luminous Emaj9 → Emaj7 close.

4.cardSummary: A → A♯°7 steps chromatically toward B bass
4.whatItDoes: Opens on warm Aadd9 (IV) and inserts chromatic passing A♯dim7 (♯iv°7) on the final beat.
4.biggerPicture: Creates the classic gospel/hymn bass climb (A → A♯ → B) into Bar 5's tonic E.
4.whyItWorks: Raising A just one fret to A♯ creates a symmetrical diminished 7th that squeezes half-step inward onto B and E.

27.cardSummary: G♯° connects E7 upward into A7
27.whatItDoes: Turns the diatonic 3rd degree into diminished G♯° (iii°), replacing G♯m's 5th D♯ with tight tritone D♮.
27.biggerPicture: Bridges E7 (Bar 26) up into bluesy A7 (Bar 28) inside Verse 2's rising gospel climax.
27.whyItWorks: Shares B, D, and G♯ with E7 (acting like a rootless E7 voicing) while stepping the bass smoothly G♯ → A.

74.cardSummary: Borrowed G6 → Fmaj7 glides down to Emaj9
74.whatItDoes: Borrows outside G6 (♭III) and Neapolitan Fmaj7 (♭II), floating colorful 6th and maj7 tones chromatically downward.
74.biggerPicture: Delivers the signature jazz/fingerstyle ending tag right before the final Emaj9 → Emaj7 tonic resolution.
74.whyItWorks: Sliding parallel chord shapes down by step and half-step (G → F → E) resolves gently onto Emaj9 via smooth half-step voice leading.

tommy-emmanuel-windy_and_warm_both.theorySummary: 84-bar alternating-thumb Travis picking standard in A Minor: grooves over open-fifth A5 & Asus4 pedal riffs, dips into bright C / F major folk warmth, and flashes surprising A Major / E7 / Bm7 blues-country colors in the middle bridge.

studyGuide.vibeAndSound: Smoky, swinging thumb-and-fingers groove—steady alternating low A/E bass line supports syncopated bluesy bends and open-string chords.
studyGuide.harmonyHook: Blends folk-minor open fifths (A5, Asus4) with a warm relative-major lift (C → F) and a bright parallel A Major / Dorian D7 turnaround bridge.
practiceTips: Lock in the alternating bass thumb pattern in Bars 1–4 before adding the upper melody syncopations.
Notice how Bars 1–20 stay grounded on A5, Asus4, and Am/C while only shifting the top chord color.
In Bars 52–65, listen for the bright parallel shift into A Major (A → A7 → Bm7 → D7) before C/E pulls back to A Minor.

sections.title: 1. Intro & Main A5/Asus4 Riff
sections.progressionTag: A5 – E5 – Am – C/E – Asus4 – Em
sections.insight: Establishes the bouncy Travis-picking thumb groove, toggling open A5 power chords, Asus4 suspensions, and Am/C/Em chord flashes.

sections.title: 2. Bass Walk & Relative Major Lift
sections.progressionTag: Am7 – Gadd9/A – Dm/F – E7 – G7 – F♯m7 – C – F – Dm
sections.insight: Steps down chromatically (A5 → Amaj7/A♭ → G7 → F♯m7 → Em/G) into warm C → F → Dm major/relative relief.

sections.title: 3. Parallel A Major Blues Bridge
sections.progressionTag: Am – A5 – A – A7 – E7 – Bm7 – D7 – Emaj7 – C/E
sections.insight: Brightens into parallel A Major and dominant A7 blues licks before Dorian D7 and Emaj7 pivot back through C/E.

sections.title: 4. Closing Groove & Open-5th Tag
sections.progressionTag: Am – C/E – Asus4 – Em – A5 – E5 – A5
sections.insight: Returns to the signature A Minor fingerstyle riff and winds down with crisp A5 → E5 alternating-bass turnarounds.

1.cardSummary: A5 → E5 power chords launch Travis thumb groove
1.whatItDoes: Opens on a lean, thirdless A5 power chord (A · E) before tipping onto E5 on the off-beat.
1.biggerPicture: Sets the rhythmic engine of Section 1 without locking down major or minor 3rds until Am enters in Bar 3.
1.whyItWorks: Leaving out the 3rd lets the open A and E strings ring crisply under percussive thumb-picked bass notes.

4.whatItDoes: Replaces Am's C with suspended 4th D (Asus4), creating open tension that relaxes onto Am/E mid-bar.
4.biggerPicture: Forms the melodic hook of the main 4-bar riff (Bars 3–4, repeated in 7–8 and 11–12).
4.whyItWorks: D sits one fret above C on the B string, so lifting one finger resolves the suspension effortlessly back into Am.

52.cardSummary: Flips A Minor bright into A Major
52.whatItDoes: Brings in bright C♯ to turn tonic A Minor into A Major (I), kicking off the sunny country-blues bridge.
52.biggerPicture: Transforms the second half of the tune (Bars 52–63) into an upbeat A Major / A7 → D7 turnaround before returning to Am.
52.whyItWorks: Sharing the exact same A and E open strings makes flipping C → C♯ sound punchy and seamless.

travis-cannonball_rag_both.theorySummary: 113-bar Merle Travis thumb-picking ragtime tour de force in G Major: powered by a roaring Circle-of-Fifths secondary-dominant chain (E [V/ii] → A7 [V7/V] → D7 [V7] → G [I]), classic C → C♯° → D7 → B♭° → Am → G ragtime turnarounds, and a walking-bass C-section bridge.

studyGuide.vibeAndSound: Lightning-fast, train-chugging acoustic ragtime—rock-steady boom-chick alternating bass drives snappy, syncopated banjo-roll licks.
studyGuide.harmonyHook: Textbook ragtime Circle-of-Fifths engine: leaps three steps clockwise to E (V/ii), then falls counter-clockwise step by step (E → A7 → D7 → G) right back home.
practiceTips: Follow the big Circle-of-Fifths wheel during Bars 2–8: watch E jump to the sharp side and march straight back clockwise-to-home (E → A7 → D7 → G).
Spot the classic ragtime turnaround in Bars 26–29 & 54–57: C → C♯dim → D7 → B♭dim → Am → G walks chromatically upward and downward.
In Section 3 (Bars 58–68), watch the bass climb stepwise A → B → C → D under Am – F♯dim/A – G/B – Am/C – D5.

sections.title: 1. A & B Themes — Circle Rag Chain
sections.progressionTag: Gmaj7 – E – A7 – Em – D7 – G – C – C♯dim – B♭dim – Am
sections.insight: Launches the signature E (V/ii) → A7 (V7/V) → D7 (V7) → G ragtime cycle, adds B7/A color, and closes with a C♯dim/B♭dim turnaround.

sections.title: 2. Theme Reprise & Rag Turnaround
sections.progressionTag: E – A7 – Em – D7 – G – C – C♯dim – B♭dim – Am – G
sections.insight: Replays the roaring secondary-dominant ragtime phrases with fresh thumb-picking momentum before returning cleanly to G.

sections.title: 3. Bridge — Walking Bass Lift
sections.progressionTag: Am – F♯dim/A – G/B – Am/C – D5 – C – C♯dim – D7
sections.insight: Walks the bass steadily up the G Major scale (A → B → C → D) through ii, vii°, I, and V5 before another ragtime turnaround.

sections.title: 4. Final Medley & Syncopated Coda
sections.progressionTag: E – A7 – D7 – G – Am – G5 – Bm7 – F♯7 – C/G
sections.insight: Sweeps through the complete A–B–C ragtime medley one last time, ending with jazzy Bm7 → F♯7 (V7/iii) → C/G sparkle.

2.cardSummary: E Major kicks off 3-step Circle-of-Fifths chain
2.whatItDoes: Jumps clockwise to E Major (V/ii), bringing in crisp G♯ outside G Major to launch the ragtime Circle-of-Fifths cycle.
2.biggerPicture: Kicks off the classic ragtime progression E (V/ii) → A7 (V7/V) → D7 (V7) → G (I) across Bars 2–8.
2.whyItWorks: E sits three fifths clockwise from G, creating high harmonic energy that resolves smoothly counter-clockwise fifth by fifth back home.

26.cardSummary: C → C♯dim squeezes bass chromatically to D7
26.whatItDoes: Follows warm subdominant C (IV) with chromatic passing C♯dim (♯iv°), raising C by one fret to C♯.
26.biggerPicture: Drives the signature ragtime turnaround (C → C♯dim → D7 → G) closing Sections 1, 2, and 3.
26.whyItWorks: The bass steps smoothly C → C♯ → D while C♯dim's diminished tritone pulls half-step inward into D7.

58.cardSummary: Starts ascending A → B → C → D bass walk
58.whatItDoes: Opens the contrasting bridge on minor ii (Am), anchoring root A before F♯dim/A, G/B, Am/C, and D5 climb upward.
58.biggerPicture: Changes the ragtime texture in Section 3 with a smooth 4-bar rising scale bass line.
58.whyItWorks: Inverting G over B and Am over C keeps each bass note adjacent by scale step (A → B → C → D), giving unstoppable forward drive.

tommy-emmanuel-classical_gas_both.theorySummary: 165-bar acoustic showstopper in A Minor (Tommy Emmanuel's arrangement): marries classical Baroque-folk motifs (Am – Gmaj7/F♯ – Em – Esus4) and bright Dorian IV (D/A, D7) lifts with dramatic brass-style modulations through C, E♭, A♭, and an uplifting parallel A Major coda.

studyGuide.vibeAndSound: Virtuosic, cinematic acoustic guitar anthem—shifting effortlessly from intimate Baroque fingerpicking to percussive flamenco-pop fanfares.
studyGuide.harmonyHook: Turns a nimble descending bass line (A → F♯ → E) and Dorian D/D7 lifts into an orchestral journey via C Major, flat-side E♭/A♭ bursts, and parallel A Major.
practiceTips: Watch the descending bass hook in Bars 1–4: Am → Gmaj7/F♯ → Em → Esus4 → Am walks A → F♯ → E → A smoothly down the strings.
Spot the bright Dorian IV color in Bars 13, 15, 33, 70, and 132: D/A and D7 raise F to F♯ for sunny acoustic pop energy.
Notice how Section 2 (Bar 45) & Section 3 (Bar 107) suddenly blast outward into flat-side chords (E♭ → Gm → A♭) before E7 snaps you back to A Minor.

sections.title: 1. Main Theme & Dorian D7
sections.progressionTag: Am – Gmaj7/F♯ – Em – Esus4 – D/A – D7 – G – B♭maj7 – E7
sections.insight: States the famous descending A Minor theme, brightens with Dorian D/D7 lifts, passes through B♭maj7 (♭II) → Bm7 → E7, and settles onto relative C Major.

sections.title: 2. Fanfare & Chromatic Excursion
sections.progressionTag: C – E♭ – Gm – A♭ – Dmaj7 – E – Am – Edim7 – Fmaj7 – E7
sections.insight: Launches bold flat-side modulations (E♭ → Gm → A♭) and Edim7 drama before climbing back through D7 → B♭maj7 → Bm7 onto a ringing E dominant plateau.

sections.title: 3. E Major Interlude & Reprise
sections.progressionTag: Bm7 – B – C♯m7 – Aadd9 – E – Fm/C – E♭ – A♭ – Am
sections.insight: Unfolds a lyrical interlude in E Major (Bm7 → B → C♯m7 → E → Aadd9), sweeps back through the E♭–A♭ fanfare, and reprises the A Minor groove.

sections.title: 4. Parallel A Major & Tag Finale
sections.progressionTag: Am – D7 – E7 – A – Asus2 – B7/A – E5 – G – Fmaj7
sections.insight: Drives the theme to a joyful parallel A Major / Asus2 climax (Bars 146–161) before descending Am7/G → G → Fmaj7 for the iconic acoustic ending.

2.cardSummary: Gmaj7/F♯ → Em walks bass F♯ down to E
2.whatItDoes: Voices natural-minor VII (Gmaj7) with its major 7th (F♯) in the bass, stepping smoothly down into Em on beat 3.
2.biggerPicture: Creates the signature falling bass hook (A → F♯ → E) linking Bar 1's Am into Bar 3's Esus4.
2.whyItWorks: F♯ acts as an active Dorian passing tone in the bass between A and E, while G and B carry right into Em.

13.cardSummary: D/A raises F to F♯ over steady A pedal
13.whatItDoes: Borrows bright Dorian IV (D Major) while keeping A anchored underneath as a pedal bass.
13.biggerPicture: Punctuates the A Minor groove with an airy, upbeat acoustic-rock lift before dropping back to Am in Bar 14.
13.whyItWorks: Swapping F for F♯ over the unchanged open A pedal creates instant major sparkle without leaving the fingerboard position.

45.cardSummary: Sudden E♭ → Gm fanfare leaps to flat side
45.whatItDoes: Steps abruptly out of C Major (Bar 44) onto flat-side E♭ Major and Gm, shifting far counter-clockwise on the Circle.
45.biggerPicture: Ignites Section 2's dramatic brass-like interlude (E♭ → Gm → A♭ → E♭/G) before E7 snaps back to A Minor.
45.whyItWorks: G stays in the inner voice as a chromatic pivot (C's 5th becomes E♭'s 3rd), smoothing a dramatic 3-flat modulation.

146.cardSummary: Flips A Minor anthem bright into A Major
146.whatItDoes: Transforms the home key from A Minor into open, triumphant A Major (I), followed by shimmering Asus2/E pedals.
146.biggerPicture: Lifts Section 4's high-energy coda into sunlit major territory before the closing Am7/G → G → Fmaj7 descent.
146.whyItWorks: Open A, B, and E strings vibrate sympathetically across A and Asus2, letting C♯ ring as a joyful surprise.

bach_bwv1007_cello_suite_1_prelude_cello.theorySummary: 42-bar solo cello masterpiece in G Major: turns rapid 16th-note string crossings (bariolage) into a complete harmonic journey—anchoring open G2, climbing clockwise through A7 → D and E7 → Am → D♯° → D7, peaking on Bar 22's D7 cadenza, and sweeping across open-A3 bariolage to G.

studyGuide.vibeAndSound: Continuous 16th-note bow crossings across open cello strings weave bass, inner harmony, and singing top melody into a single golden line.
studyGuide.harmonyHook: A masterclass in Circle of Fifths navigation: anchors home with I–IVmaj7–Imaj7–I over open G2, climbs clockwise via A7 → D and E7 → Am, and resolves home via G7 → C.
practiceTips: Memorize Bars 1–4 first: the open G2 C/G string stays anchored on every downbeat while upper voices outline G → Cmaj7/G → Gmaj7 → G.
Watch the Circle wheel in Bars 6–15: Bach steps clockwise to D via A7/C♯ (V7/V), then pivots through E7/D (V7/ii) and D♯dim (♯v°) back to D7.
In Bars 31–36, keep the bow loose crossing against the open A3 string while the left hand walks stepwise down D and C strings.

sections.title: 1. Opening G2 Pedal
sections.progressionTag: G – Cmaj7/G – Gmaj7 – G
sections.insight: Establishes G Major over an open G2 bass drone, rocking between I and IVmaj7/G and gentle F♯ shimmer before departing in Bar 5.

sections.title: 2. Circle Climb to D & Em
sections.progressionTag: G/B – A7/C♯ – D – Em – E7/D – Am/C – D♯dim – D7/F♯
sections.insight: Climbs clockwise around the Circle via A7/C♯ (V7/V) into D Major, detours through Em and E7/D (V7/ii) → Am, and squeezes D♯dim back to D7.

sections.title: 3. V7/IV Return & D7 Cadenza
sections.progressionTag: G7 – C/G – Gmaj7 – F♯m7/C♯ – D7 – A7 – D7
sections.insight: Adds F♮ to turn G into G7 (V7/IV → C/G), then settles onto an extended 5-bar D7 dominant cadenza (Bars 21–25) before climbing again.

sections.title: 4. Open-A Bariolage & Finale
sections.progressionTag: F♯m7/A – D – Bm7 – Am7 – D – Dm – G/D – Dsus4 – D7 – G
sections.insight: Crosses rapidly against the ringing open A3 string across Bars 31–36, darkens momentarily via Dm (v), and builds Dsus4 → D7 to a resounding final G chord.

1.whatItDoes: Anchors G Major (I) on the lowest open G2 string while upper 16ths arpeggiate B and D in cello bariolage.
1.biggerPicture: Establishes the resonant open-G2 bass pedal spanning Bars 1–2 and sets up the opening 4-bar tonic frame.
1.whyItWorks: Because G2 rings freely on an open string, every bow crossing sounds like two cellos—bass drone plus singing melody.

6.cardSummary: A7/C♯ climbs half-step C♯ → D into V
6.whatItDoes: Secondary dominant V7/V (A7/C♯) introduces chromatic C♯ directly in the bass (1st inversion) to propel toward D.
6.biggerPicture: Steps clockwise from G/B (Bar 5) onto D Major (Bar 7), launching Section 2's tonal excursion.
6.whyItWorks: The cello bass climbs cleanly B → C♯ → D by half-step while A7's C♯–G tritone collapses straight into D–F♯.

13.cardSummary: D♯dim squeezes D♯ → E between Am chords
13.whatItDoes: Injects sharp diminished tension (D♯dim = ♯v° / leading tone to Em) right inside the A Minor sequence.
13.biggerPicture: Connects Am/C (Bar 12) cleanly into Am7/E → Am7/G (Bar 14) on the way back to D7.
13.whyItWorks: Chromatic D♯ sits one semitone below E, giving the melody razor-sharp Baroque pull into Bar 14.

22.cardSummary: Holds dramatic D7 cadenza before resolution
22.whatItDoes: Sustains dominant V7 (D7/A) in the middle of the cello's dramatic cascading scale flourish.
22.biggerPicture: Marks the famous structural midpoint climax of the Prelude (Bars 21–25) before spinning back toward G in Bar 25.
22.whyItWorks: Suspending D7 over alternating bass tones (C → A → D → F♯) builds enormous harmonic pressure to resolve home.

saint_saens_le_cygne_the_swan_cello.theorySummary: 27-bar Romantic cello cantabile in G Major (6/4): floats a serene singing line (G → Gmaj7 → Am7/G → Em) over rippling piano-inspired arpeggios, dips gracefully into minor color (Gm → F♯7 → Bm → Fm → C7 → Fmaj7), and glides back onto a tranquil G Major close.

studyGuide.vibeAndSound: Pure Romantic cantabile—long, singing legato phrases on the cello's A and D strings gliding effortlessly like a swan over calm water.
studyGuide.harmonyHook: Teaches subtle chromatic darkening: borrows parallel Gm (i) in Bar 7 so F♯7 (V7/iii) can lift into B Minor (iii), then drifts flat-side (Fm → C7 → Fmaj7) before returning to G.
practiceTips: Follow Bars 1–4 closely: the bass holds G across G → Gmaj7 → Am7/G (an unbroken G pedal) before gently releasing to Em.
Notice the harmonic magic in Bar 7: dropping B to B♭ turns G Major into Gm for two beats, smoothly pivoting via F♯7 into B Minor (Bar 9).
Trace the romantic flat-side sequence in Bars 12–14: Am → Fm/G♯ → C7/G → Fmaj7 steps down chromatically before D7 brings you back home.

sections.title: 1. Serene G Theme & Gm Shadow
sections.progressionTag: G – Gmaj7 – Am7/G – Em – G – Gm – F♯7
sections.insight: Floats the famous melody over a G pedal (Bars 1–3), reprises it in Bars 5–6, then turns suddenly dark via parallel Gm → F♯7 (V7/iii).

sections.title: 2. B Minor & Romantic Flat Sequence
sections.progressionTag: Bm/F♯ – F♯7 – Bm – D7 – Fm/G♯ – C7 – Fmaj7 – D
sections.insight: Visits B Minor (iii), cascades through tender flat-side harmony (Fm/G♯ → C7 → Fmaj7), and pivots through Dm/A into D7 (V7).

sections.title: 3. Lyrical Reprise & Peaceful Close
sections.progressionTag: G – Am7/G – Em – E7 – Am – F♯dim/A – G/B – Em7 – G/D
sections.insight: Glides back into the G Major opening motif, enriches it with E7 (V7/ii) → Am → F♯dim/A, and drifts softly out across Em7 and G/D.

2.cardSummary: F♯ warms G into Gmaj7 over G pedal
2.whatItDoes: Expands G Major into lush Gmaj7 (Imaj7), letting the cello float on singing F♯ while the G pedal holds below.
2.biggerPicture: Bridges opening tonic G (Bar 1) toward Am7/G (Bar 3) on the initial 3-bar G pedal.
2.whyItWorks: Half-step tension between F♯ and root G gives the melody yearning beauty without disturbing the calm bass.

7.cardSummary: Gm darkens Bar 6; F♯7 pivots toward Bm
7.whatItDoes: Flips bright G Major into parallel Gm (introducing B♭), then fires F♯7 (V7/iii) mid-bar with chromatic A♯.
7.biggerPicture: Triggers the swan's emotional turning point, modulating smoothly from G Major out to B Minor (iii) in Bars 8–9.
7.whyItWorks: D acts as a shared tone bridging Gm and F♯7, while F♯7's A♯–E tritone resolves cleanly into Bm (B–D–F♯).

13.cardSummary: C7/G chains from Fm toward Fmaj7
13.whatItDoes: Follows borrowed Fm/G♯ (Bar 12) with bluesy/dominant C7 (IV7), pulling flatward via chromatic B♭.
13.biggerPicture: Steers the middle development cleanly onto remote Fmaj7 (♭VIImaj7) in Bar 14 before D Major re-centers G.
13.whyItWorks: Fm/G♯ (A♭) steps down half-step in the bass to C7/G (G) → Fmaj7 (F), keeping every voice close together.

corelli_op3_no1_grave_violin.theorySummary: 19-bar Baroque trio-sonata Grave in F Major: showcases Corelli's signature 'chain of suspensions' and walking bass lines (I–V–IV–I), weaving vi7–iii7 voice exchanges, V7/vi tonicizations (A7 → B♭), and broad plagal/authentic cadences.

studyGuide.vibeAndSound: Noble, unhurried Baroque violin poise—overlapping voices lean across barlines like a slow cathedral conversation.
studyGuide.harmonyHook: Masterclass in Baroque bass counterpoint: stepwise 1st-inversion chords (F/A, B♭/D, Em/B) keep the low end singing while Circle-of-Fifths chains pull gently forward.
practiceTips: Listen to Bars 1–4: notice how F → Gm7 → C → F/A → B♭ → F/C → F weaves smoothly through 1st and 2nd inversions rather than static root jumps.
Follow Bars 9–12: Corelli confirms F Major in Bars 9–10, then slips through Em/B → Dm → A7 (V7/vi) → B♭/D for classic Baroque expressiveness.
In Bars 15–19, hear the rising bass line F/A → Gm/B♭ → F/C → B♭ → C → F carry the final cadence grandly home.

sections.title: 1. Baroque Opening & F Cadence
sections.progressionTag: F – Gm7 – C – F/A – B♭ – F/C – Dm7/F – C7 – F
sections.insight: Presents the stately F Major theme over walking inversions (F/A, F/C), touches vi7–iii7 counterpoint in Bar 7, and closes firmly with C7 → F.

sections.title: 2. Applied A7 & Grand Closing Cadence
sections.progressionTag: C7 – F/A – Em/B – Dm – A7 – B♭/D – B♭maj7 – C – F
sections.insight: Pivots via Em/B → Dm into secondary dominant A7 (V7/vi), resolves deceptively onto B♭/D, and builds an ascending bass line (F/A → Gm/B♭ → F/C → C → F) home.

7.cardSummary: Dm7/F → Am7/E walks bass down F → E
7.whatItDoes: Links relative minor Dm7 (vi7) and mediant Am7 (iii7) through smooth 1st/3rd inversions.
7.biggerPicture: Creates Corelli's hallmark Baroque sigh right before the Bar 8–9 C7 → F cadence.
7.whyItWorks: F steps down to E in the bass while A and C hold steady as shared tones between Dm7 and Am7.

12.whatItDoes: Introduces raised C♯ inside secondary dominant A7 (V7/vi), pointing strongly toward D Minor (Dm).
12.biggerPicture: Instead of landing on Dm, surprises the ear with 1st-inversion B♭/D (IV), keeping the closing phrase airborne.
12.whyItWorks: C♯ steps up a half-step to D (B♭'s 3rd in the bass) while A stays anchored—so B♭/D fulfills the melodic pull smoothly.

massenet_thais_meditation_violin.theorySummary: 71-bar Romantic solo violin showpiece in D Major: floats an ecstatic opening melody (D → G → Em → A7), borrows melancholic flat-VII (C) and V/ii (B) colors, climbs through remote flat keys (C7 → F → A♯m) to an A♯dim climax, and dissolves into shimmering harmonic echoes (C♯7, D♯7 → D).

studyGuide.vibeAndSound: Rapturous, glowing Romantic violin lyricism—slow, singing arches build from tender prayer to passionate height and back to hushed serenity.
studyGuide.harmonyHook: Shows how Romantic composers stretch a simple D Major melody: borrowing Mixolydian ♭VII (C) and V/ii (B → Em), modulating briefly up to F Major and A♯m/B♭m, and closing with delicate chromatic neighbors (C♯7, D♯7).
practiceTips: In Bars 6–10, hear the classic D Major song progression (G → Em → A7 → D) turn bittersweet in Bar 14–16 via C (♭VII) → B (V/ii) → Em.
Trace the dramatic middle storm in Bars 27–38: C → C7 → F/C → Am → A♯m → A7 → A♯dim leaps boldly to the flat side before A7 pulls home to D.
In the coda (Bars 58–71), savor the magical side-steps around tonic D: C♯7 (Bar 59) and D♯7 → Gdim/A♯ (Bar 61) kiss D from a half-step below and above.

sections.title: 1. D Major Prayer & ♭VII–V/ii Turn
sections.progressionTag: D – G – Em – A7 – C – B – Em – Bsus4 – A7 – D
sections.insight: States the famous soaring D Major theme over gentle D/A bass oscillations, adding poignant color via Mixolydian C (♭VII) and B (V/ii) → Em → A7.

sections.title: 2. Passionate Flat-Side Climax
sections.progressionTag: C – F♯7 – Em – A7 – C7 – F/C – A♯m – A7 – A♯dim – G
sections.insight: Surges upward through F♯7 (V7/vi), modulates boldly via C7 → F Major into remote A♯m/B♭m, and peaks on A7 → A♯dim → G → C♯dim before D returns.

sections.title: 3. Ecstatic Theme Reprise
sections.progressionTag: D – G – Em – A7 – C/G – B – Em – Bsus4 – A7 – D
sections.insight: Reclaims the soaring D Major prayer at full romantic intensity, sweeping cleanly back through the C → B → Em → A7 arc.

sections.title: 4. Chromatic Neighbours & Coda
sections.progressionTag: C♯7 – D – D♯7 – Gdim/A♯ – D – G/B – F♯/A♯ – A7 – D
sections.insight: Floats gently around tonic D using half-step dominant neighbors (C♯7 below, D♯7 above), a warm F♯/A♯ → A7 cadence, and quiet final D chords.

14.cardSummary: C Major (♭VII) softens D Major with C♮
14.whatItDoes: Replaces D Major's sharp leading tone C♯ with warm C♮, introducing flat-VII (C/E → C/G) color.
14.biggerPicture: Creates the tender aching turn in Section 1 leading straight into B (V/ii) and Em in Bars 15–16.
14.whyItWorks: Lowering C♯ to C♮ creates a descending chromatic sigh (D → C♯ → C♮ → B) straight into Bar 15's B chord.

36.cardSummary: A7 → A♯dim pushes chromatically toward peak
36.whatItDoes: Paired after A7 (V7), A♯dim (♯v°) squeezes the bass chromatically up (A → A♯) at the climax of the storm.
36.biggerPicture: Marks the emotional peak of Section 2 before A7 releases back through G → C♯dim onto D Major in Bar 40.
36.whyItWorks: Stepping the bass just one half-step upward from A to A♯ turns stable dominant tension into urgent upward yearning.

59.cardSummary: C♯7 kisses D from a half-step below
59.whatItDoes: Places dominant C♯7 (V7/iii) directly between two D Major chords before stepping its 7th (B) down to A.
59.biggerPicture: Opens the dreamy coda's half-step harmonic halos (C♯7 below D in Bar 59, D♯7 above D in Bar 61).
59.whyItWorks: C♯ and E♯ sit a single half-step below D and F♯, so resolving C♯7 straight up onto D Major feels weightless and shimmering.

mozart_k156_mvt2_adagio_violin.theorySummary: 88-bar Classical slow-movement quartet gem in E Minor (Adagio): contrasts poignant E Minor sighs (Em/G → B7/D♯) against luminous G Major (III) cantabile periods, then ventures through Neapolitan Fdim/G♯, A♯m, and F♯7/C♯ harmonic drama before a hushed recapitulation.

studyGuide.vibeAndSound: Intimate, tearful Classical chamber Adagio—sighing two-note motifs and delicate 1st-inversion suspensions carry Mozart's hallmark singing elegance.
studyGuide.harmonyHook: Textbook sonata-form minor-key architecture: establishes E Minor via Em/G → B7/D♯, lifts smoothly to relative G Major (III) via A7 → D7, and explores chromatic diminished/V7/V drama in the development.
practiceTips: Notice the opening 2-bar sigh (Em/G → B7/D♯): putting G in the bass and D♯ in the bass makes the progression glide rather than thud on root chords.
Follow the sunny lift into G Major (III) starting at Bar 5: D7 → G (Bars 10–14) temporarily makes G feel like home.
In the development (Bars 29–50), watch how Fdim/G♯, A♯m, and F♯7 (V7/V) pull tension sharply before B7 resolves back to Em.

sections.title: 1. Exposition — Em to G Major
sections.progressionTag: Em/G – B7/D♯ – B7 – G – Cmaj7 – A7 – D7 – G
sections.insight: Opens in tragic E Minor (Em/G → B7/D♯), then blooms into relative G Major (III) via Cmaj7 and an A7 → D7 → G cadence.

sections.title: 2. Exposition Repeat
sections.progressionTag: Em/G – B7/D♯ – B7 – G – Cmaj7 – A7 – D7 – G
sections.insight: Repeats the lyrical E Minor → G Major exposition period, anchoring the bright G Major close before the development turns dark.

sections.title: 3. Chromatic Development
sections.progressionTag: Fdim/G♯ – G7/B – A♯m – Bm – F♯7/C♯ – B/D♯ – Edim/A♯ – C7/E
sections.insight: Weaves Neapolitan Fdim/G♯, rising chromatic A♯m → Bm, and urgent F♯7 (V7/V) → B7 turns to drive back to E Minor in Bars 45–51.

sections.title: 4. Recapitulation & Quiet Close
sections.progressionTag: Em/G – B7/D♯ – G – Fdim/G♯ – F♯7/C♯ – B/D♯ – Em/B – Em
sections.insight: Reprises the full thematic journey with heightened chromatic urgency (Bars 66–86) before settling calmly onto pure E Minor in Bar 88.

2.cardSummary: B7/D♯ puts leading tone D♯ in bass toward Em
2.whatItDoes: Voices dominant B7 in 1st inversion, putting E Minor's raised leading tone D♯ in the bass with the D♯–A tritone.
2.biggerPicture: Creates the aching Classical sigh following Bar 1's Em/G before B7 shifts into root-position push in Bars 3–4.
2.whyItWorks: F♯ and B stay closely connected while D♯ (a half-step below E) pulls urgently upward toward tonic E.

10.cardSummary: D7 (V7/III) locks in bright G Major arrival
10.whatItDoes: Fires dominant D7 (V7/III) right after A7 (Bar 9), resolving straight onto relative major G (III).
10.biggerPicture: Completes the Exposition's classic minor-to-relative-major modulation (Em → G Major) spanning Bars 5–14.
10.whyItWorks: D7's tritone (F♯ and C) pulls inward into G and B, dropping cleanly counter-clockwise by 5th on the Circle of Fifths.

29.cardSummary: Fdim/G♯ jolts out of G Major into development
29.whatItDoes: Introduces Neapolitan/chromatic diminished Fdim/G♯ (♭ii°) with borrowed F♮ before stepping onto Am (iv).
29.biggerPicture: Shatters Bar 28's serene G Major close to launch Mozart's turbulent harmonic development.
29.whyItWorks: Fdim's G♯ bass walks by half-step directly into A Minor (G♯ → A), turning shock into smooth voice leading.
